facts.statement: The genus Metriorhynchus was established by Christian von Meyer in 1832.
facts.quote: parent_authority: von Meyer, 1832

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Metriorhynchus brevirostris.
facts.quote: species: brevirostris

facts.statement: The type species M. brevirostris was originally named in 1829 as a species of Steneosaurus before being elevated to a separate genus in 1832.
facts.quote: The type species, M. brevirostris was named in 1829 as a species of Steneosaurus before being named as a separate genus by the German palaeontologist Christian von Meyer in 1832.

facts.statement: Fossil specimens of Metriorhynchus are known from Kimmeridgian deposits in France.
facts.quote: Fossil specimens referrable to Metriorhynchus are known from Kimmeridgian (Late Jurassic) deposits of France.

facts.statement: Young et al. (2019) synonymized M. geoffroyii with M. brevirostris and reassigned MNHN.F.RJN 116 to M. brevirostris.
facts.quote: Young et al. (2019) also synonymised M. geoffroyii with M. brevirostris and reassigned MNHN.F.RJN 116 to M. brevirostris.

facts.statement: Only one valid species is currently recognized, the type species M. brevirostris (formerly M. geoffroyii).
facts.quote: Only one valid species is recognized today, the type species M. geoffroyii (now called M. brevirostris).

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses do not support the monophyly of Metriorhynchus, a view held from the 1860s to 2010.
facts.quote: Recent phylogenetic analyses however, do not support the monophyly of Metriorhynchus, as believed during the 1860s-2010.

facts.statement: Adams-Tresman (1987) used linear morphometrics to find only two species from the Oxford Clay: M. superciliosus and M. brachyrhynchus.
facts.quote: However, Adams-Tresman (1987), using linear morphometrics, could only distinguish between the two skull groups, so she found there to be two species from the Oxford Clay, M. superciliosus and M. brachyrhynchus.

facts.statement: Metriorhynchus belonged to the Metriorhynchidae, a group with tail anatomy indicating a shark-like tail fluke.
facts.quote: It was a member of the Metriorhynchidae, a group of thalattosuchians with a tail anatomy which indicates that they had a tail fluke similar to that of a shark.

facts.statement: Unlike many pseudosuchians, Metriorhynchus lacked extensive osteoderms and likely had smoother skin similar to plesiosaurs and ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Unlike many other pseudosuchians, they did not have extensive osteoderms covering the body. Instead it appears that they had smoother skin similar to other marine reptiles like plesiosaurs and ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: Metriorhynchids had hip anatomy conducive for live birth, a trait evidenced in the related Dakosaurus.
facts.quote: Metriorhynchids also had a hip anatomy conducive for live birth and evidence from the related Dakosaurus does show that they did this.

facts.statement: It has been speculated that Metriorhynchus attacked weak individuals of Leedsichthys, as featured in documentaries like Sea Monsters.
facts.quote: The idea of Metriorhynchus attacking weak Leedsichthys individuals has been speculated to be the case in the past such as in the BBC and Discovery Channel documentary Sea Monsters.

facts.statement: Metriorhynchus was a predator that spent most, if not all, of its life in the sea.
facts.quote: Metriorhynchus fue un depredador que pasó la mayor parte de su vida, si no toda, en el mar.

facts.statement: No eggs or nests of Metriorhynchus have been found, so its life cycle is largely unknown, unlike other Mesozoic marine reptiles like plesiosaurs and ichthyosaurs known to give live birth at sea.
facts.quote: No se han hallado huevos o nidos de Metriorhynchus o de alguno de sus parientes próximos, por lo que se desconoce mucho del ciclo vital de este animal, a diferencia de otros grandes reptiles marinos del Mesozoico, como los plesiosaurios o los ictiosaurios de los cuales se sabe que daban a luz crías vivas en el mar.

facts.statement: It is currently unknown whether Metriorhynchus performed mating on land or in the sea.
facts.quote: Asimismo, se desconoce actualmente donde el Metriorhynchus realizaba su apareamiento, si en tierra o en el mar.

facts.statement: Studies published since 2010 found that short-snouted metriorhynchines previously assigned to Metriorhynchus are distinct genera.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estudios publicados desde 2010 han encontrado que las brevirostrina metriorhynchines referidas a Metriorhynchus son géneros distintos por derecho propio

facts.statement: Two long-snouted species, M. acutus and M. leedsi, have been reclassified into the genus Gracilineustes.
facts.quote: Dos especies longirostrinas, M. acutus y M. leedsi han sido reclasificadas en el género Gracilineustes

facts.statement: All short-snouted species have recently been transferred to the genera Purranisaurus and Suchodus.
facts.quote: Todas las especies brevirostrinas han sido recientemente transferidas a los géneros Purranisaurus y Suchodus

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses do not support the genus Metriorhynchus as a monophyletic group.
facts.quote: Análisis filogenéticos más recientes, sin embargo no apoyan la monofilia del género Metriorhynchus

facts.statement: However, some long-snouted forms appear to form a natural group.
facts.quote: No obstante, algunas de las formas longirostrinas sí parecen formar un grupo natural

facts.statement: Metriorhynchus averaged about 3 meters in length, similar in size to many modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: Con cerca de 3 metros de longitud en promedio, Metriorhynchus era de un tamaño similar al de muchos cocodrilos modernos

facts.statement: It had a much more streamlined and tapered body with a finned tail, making it a much more efficient swimmer than modern crocodile species.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, poseía un cuerpo mucho más estilizado y ahusado, junto con una cola provista de aleta al final, haciéndolo un nadador mucho más eficiente que las especies modernas de cocodrilos

facts.statement: Recent examination of fossil specimens of M. superciliosus showed adults had well-developed glands to eliminate excess salt from their bodies.
facts.quote: Un examen reciente de los especímenes fósiles de la especie Metriorhynchus superciliosus han mostrado que los adultos tenían glándulas bien desarrolladas para eliminar el exceso de sal de sus cuerpos

facts.statement: This means that, like its relative Geosaurus, it was likely able to drink seawater and eat prey with the same ionic concentration as the surrounding seawater without dehydrating.
facts.quote: Esto significa que como su pariente Geosaurus debió ser capaz de consumir agua de mar (algo necesario para un animal pelágico) y devorar presas que tenían la misma concentración iónica que el agua de mar circundante

facts.statement: Metriorhynchus was a versatile and opportunistic predator, hunting armored belemnites, fast and elusive fish, and larger species like the filter-feeder Leedsichthys.
facts.quote: Metriorhynchus fue un depredador versátil y oportunista, cazando tanto belemnites acorazados, como peces rápidos y escurridizos y especies más grandes como el pez filtrador Leedsichthys

facts.statement: It occasionally likely tried to capture flying animals like pterosaurs and fed on plesiosaur carcasses on the sea floor.
facts.quote: Ocasionalmente debió tratar de capturar animales voladores como los pterosaurios así como alimentarse de cadáveres de plesiosaurios en el suelo marino

facts.statement: Despite being an effective predator, it remained vulnerable to larger predators of its time, such as the pliosaur Liopleurodon, which could reach over 10 meters in length.
facts.quote: A pesar de que el Metriorhynchus era un depredador efectivo, no dejaba de ser vulnerable a los mayores depredadores de su tiempo como el pliosaurio Liopleurodon, el cual podía llegar a medir algo más de 10 metros de longitud

facts.statement: Because it had lost the osteoderms (bony shields) characteristic of other crocodiles to become more efficient swimmers, it likely had few natural defenses against larger marine predators.
facts.quote: Dado que el Metriorhynchus había perdido ya los osteodermos (escudos óseos) característicos de otros cocodrilos, para volverse nadadores más eficientes, debió haber tenido pocas defensas naturales contra depredadores marinos mayores

facts.statement: The genus lived from the Bathonian to the Tithonian stages, between 168.2 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Tithonian (168.2 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 30 recorded fossil occurrences of the genus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 30

facts.statement: Hua & Tabouelle (2026) identified a skull from Kimmeridgian strata at Cap de la Hève in Normandy, France, as belonging to the species M. palpebrosus.
facts.quote: Hua & Tabouelle (2026) identify a skull of a member of the genus Metriorhynchus from the Kimmeridgian strata from Cap de la Hève (Normandy, France) as belonging to a member of the species M. palpebrosus
